Relevant text: when the allocated space is too small, creating an instance fails; allocate a new range with 'gcloud compute addresses create ... --global --purpose=VPC_PEERING --prefix-length=16 ... --network', list the ranges already on the connection (reservedPeeringRanges), then 'gcloud services vpc-peerings update --service=servicenetworking.googleapis.com --ranges=RESERVED_RANGE_NAME,EXISTING_RANGES_LIST'. The same private services access connection serves Cloud SQL and Memorystore; the exact creation error text and that an overlap with routes learned from on-premises breaks reachability are from memory (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. The loyalty launch needs a Cloud SQL instance and a Memorystore instance on private IP in the shared VPC prod-vpc. Both creations fail. The launch's deployment pipeline must finish by 15:00 for the 15:30 announcement.
handover: prod-vpc's private services access connection has one allocated range, psa-1 (10.40.0.0/24), from 2023.
On-premises networks reach prod-vpc over Interconnect and advertise 10.0.0.0/12 and 172.16.0.0/16; the IPAM sheet lists 10.48.0.0/16 as free for Google Cloud.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows prod-vpc, the private services access peering and its allocated ranges, and on-premises routes.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The launch pipeline must finish by 15:00, 110 minutes after the failure; the instances take about 20 minutes to create once there is room.

writeup.question: For the record: why the services could not be created, which range you added and why that one, and what you recorded.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: 'Couldn't find free blocks in allocated IP ranges': prod-vpc's private services connection had one /24, psa-1, fully used by 12 managed instances.

parts.label: Range
parts.modelAnswer: Allocated psa-2 = 10.48.0.0/20 from the block reserved for Google Cloud and updated the connection with psa-1 and psa-2. 10.10.0.0/16 would have overlapped the Lyon plant.

parts.label: Recorded
parts.modelAnswer: psa-2 is in the IPAM sheet, advertised to on-premises, and alerted at 80% use.

expertPath.text: Error: no free blocks; psa-1 /24 full; on-premises owns 10.0.0.0/12; IPAM: 10.48.0.0/16 free.
psa-2 10.48.0.0/20; update with both ranges; re-run; record, advertise, alert.

overlap.headline: Free in the VPC is not free in the company
overlap.body: Private services ranges must not overlap on-premises space. Take the block your IP plan reserves for Google Cloud.

launchPostponed.headline: Managed services need room in the peering
launchPostponed.body: Private services access hands out addresses only from allocated ranges. Allocate another range and add it to the connection alongside the existing one.

expanded.headline: Good: capacity added without collisions
expanded.body: You read the error and the range's use, checked on-premises routes and the IP plan, added a non-overlapping range alongside the existing one, verified reachability, and recorded and advertised it.

scoring.modelReasoning: The managed services cannot find free addresses because the only private services range, a /24, is full. Allocate another range and add it to the connection together with the existing one. Choose it from the block the IP plan reserves for Google Cloud, not from on-premises space such as 10.10.0.0/16, which would overlap a plant. Retrying changes nothing. Record, advertise and monitor the new range.
